newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor says city to sue tobacco industry.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor says city to sue tobacco industry.

text.p: New York, the nation's most populous city, joined the nationwide battle against the tobacco industry Thursday by suing to recoup health care costs of smokers.

The suit, filed in New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan, seeks restitution and punitive damages to be determined at trial. Among allegations is that the industry violated the state's deceptive trade practices laws.
New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who has long supported smoking control efforts, is planning a news conference in the afternoon to release further details of the suit.

"The City will seek recovery of the cost of treating lung cancer and other tobacco-related diseseas in Medicaid patients and uninsured patients treated without charge in public hospitals," Giuliani's office said in a statement.
The suit is similar to those brought by 16 states in an attempt to force cigarette companies to reimburse them for health care costs of smokers.
San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Jose and 10 other counties in California have also sued the industry.
The tobacco industry criticised the mayor for filing suit.
"It would appear that Mayor Giuliani has conferred only with rabid antismokers and product liability lawyers before filing today's suit," said R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. in a statement.

"We regret that he didn't ask the tobacco industry at the very least to sit down and discuss the litigation before suing us," Reynolds said, adding that it believed there was a serious question about whether Giuliani has jurisdiction to bring such a case.
"The mayor may garner some political mileage out of this filing, but that will be all," Reynolds said.

New York City, which has a population of about 7.8 million, will be the first city on the East coast to sue the tobacco industry. Erie County, which includes the city of Buffalo, previously said it expects to file a Medicaid suit shortly and has been attempting to get other New York counties to join with it.

A group of health organisations, known as the Coalition for a Smoke-Free City, has been urging the mayor to file suit due to inaction by New York state Attorney General Dennis Vacco. A spokesman for Vacco had no immediate comment.

"The tobacco cartel has lied and misled the public about the dangers of tobacco addiction for decades. New York City's health care bill attributed to tobacco addiction exceeds $2 billion annually," the coalition said in a letter to Giuliani.
"Recovering these costs from the tobacco cartel would be popular, fair and a major boost to the City's treasury," it said.

Richard Daynard, chairman of the Tobacco Products Liablity Project at Northeastern University in Boston, said the filing by New York City is significant because it shows that leaders of the biggest states and cities can no longer ignore efforts to seek reimbursement of health care costs of smokers.
"A public official today cannot refrain from collecting available funds for defraying this expense," Daynard said.
